request: Let admins upload a CSV to bulk-create users.

labels.why: How the import behaves when some rows are bad is the requested behaviour's own error conduct.
The HTTP response to the upload, including per-row failures, is part of the requested behaviour.
Users are keyed by email in the existing store, so conflicts with existing users and within the file are a boundary the import must settle.
The request introduces an admin distinction, so a safe import must say whether a file can grant it: a privilege-escalation security check.
Who may use the import (admins only) is stated by the request and is a 'who may use it' question.
Rejecting malformed files (header, required or unexpected columns) is the import's own input validation.
Parsing BOMs, line endings and quoted fields correctly is needed for any correct CSV import with no parser dependency.

labels.applies_part: Whether users created from earlier rows stay in the store when a later row fails must be settled.
labels.why: Earlier in-store creations apply; invitations already sent need mail, which the program lacks.
A size or row limit on the upload and the error above it is a quota and boundary of the endpoint.
Empty, header-only and single-row files are edge cases of the requested behaviour.
Re-uploading the same file follows from the duplicate rule and must be stated for the import's conduct.
Background processing and completion notification need job and notification capabilities the program lacks and the request does not ask for.
The program sends no mail and the request does not ask for invitations.

labels.applies_part: What record a created user gets in the existing store (assigned id, name, email) must be settled.
labels.why: The stored shape applies; passwords, pending state and first sign-in need a sign-in capability the program lacks.

labels.applies_part: That the uploaded personal data is processed in memory and not retained after the request (its retention) must be stated.
labels.why: Retention is rigour; storing files for later download is a capability nobody asked for.
Users have only name and email, and the request does not say whether the file carries any date or number values.
The program has no logging or audit store and the request does not ask for an audit trail.
Cancelling a running import and retrying selected rows need job and import-history features the request does not ask for.

labels.applies_part: A bound on how long processing a maximum-size file in the request may take must be settled.
labels.why: The time bound is rigour; visible progress needs a progress or background capability the program lacks.
Keeping the existing users and the existing endpoints' behaviour intact is what of the existing program must be preserved.
Handling hostile values (formula injection, very long fields) is a security check on the import's input and output.
